facts.value: DeepSeek-V4: two MoE LLMs, 1M-token context. Pro: 1.6T total / 49B activated, 61 layers, d=7168. Flash: 284B total / 13B activated, 43 layers, d=4096. Pretrained on 32T (Flash) / 33T (Pro) tokens. arXiv 2606.19348, submitted 2026-04-26.
facts.source: arXiv 2606.19348 abstract + Sec 4.2.1 Model Setups (p24-25), read in the PDF 2026-09-08
facts.boundary: architecture and training-budget description, not our measurement

facts.value: Hybrid attention = CSA (Compressed Sparse Attention) + HCA (Heavily Compressed Attention), interleaved after the first 2 layers. Flash first 2 layers are pure SWA; Pro first 2 layers are HCA. CSA: KV compression m=4 (every 4 tokens -> 1 entry, overlapped grouping draws from 2m=8 neighbors), Lightning Indexer selects top-k compressed entries per query (indexer heads n_h^I=64, dim c^I=128), top-k=512 (Flash) / 1024 (Pro), MQA core, grouped output projection. HCA: aggressive compression m'=128, dense attention (no sparse selection). Both: n_h query heads (64 Flash / 128 Pro), head dimension c=512 (both models), query compression dimension d_c=1024 (Flash) / 1536 (Pro), output groups g=8 (Flash) / 16 (Pro), group dim d_g=1024, SWA branch n_win=128 recent uncompressed KV entries.
facts.source: arXiv 2606.19348 Sec 2.3 (Hybrid Attention) + Sec 4.2.1 (p24-25), read in the PDF 2026-09-08
facts.uncertainty: vendor-reported; hyperparameters stated in Sec 4.2.1, mechanism in Sec 2.3

facts.value: Partial RoPE: applied to the last 64 dimensions of queries, compressed KV entries, and core-attention outputs. Because KV entries double as values, outputs carry absolute position; the fix is RoPE with position -i on the last 64 dims of each attention output so the result encodes relative position. KV storage: BF16 for the RoPE dims, FP8 for the rest (nearly halves KV cache vs pure BF16); lightning-indexer attention in FP4. NoPE is not used anywhere in the model.
facts.source: arXiv 2606.19348 Sec 2.3.3 (Other Details: Partial Rotary Positional Embedding) + Sec 2.3.4, read 2026-09-08
facts.boundary: design description; the NoPE/RoPE break with our checkpoints is in dsv4.nope_rope_break

facts.value: MoE in every layer except the first 3 (which use Hash routing: targets from a predefined hash of the input token ID). Each MoE layer: 1 shared expert + routed experts, top-6 routed activated per token. Flash: 256 routed experts, intermediate hidden 2048. Pro: 384 routed experts, intermediate hidden 3072. Affinity scoring Sqrt(Softplus(.)) (not Sigmoid); auxiliary-loss-free load balancing + a slight sequence-wise balance loss (bias update speed 0.001, balance loss weight 0.0001); the constraint on the number of routing target nodes is removed. MTP depth 1 (same as V3, unmodified).
facts.source: arXiv 2606.19348 Sec 2.1 (Designs Inherited from V3) + Sec 4.2.1 (p24-25), read 2026-09-08

facts.value: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC): residual stream expanded by factor n_hc=4 (n_hc residual branches). Three mappings per layer: input A (1 x n_hc), residual B (n_hc x n_hc), output C (n_hc x 1); update X_{l+1} = B_l X_l + C_l F_l(A_l X_l). B constrained to doubly-stochastic (Birkhoff polytope, spectral norm <= 1, non-expansive) via Sinkhorn-Knopp with t_max=20 iterations; A and C non-negative via Sigmoid (C = 2*sigma). Dynamic parameterization: A/B/C generated from the normalized layer input via learnable W^pre/W^res/W^post plus static biases, gated by learnable alphas initialized small.

At 1M-token context vs DeepSeek-V3.2: Pro needs 27% of single-token inference FLOPs and 10% of KV cache; Flash needs 10% of FLOPs and 7% of KV cache. Against a BF16 GQA8 (head dim 128) baseline, KV cache falls to ~2% at 1M context. Enablers: mixed-precision KV (BF16 RoPE dims + FP8 rest), FP4 lightning-indexer attention, smaller attention top-k than V3.2.
facts.boundary: relative efficiency claims, not our measurement

facts.value: Muon optimizer for the majority of parameters (momentum 0.95, weight decay 0.1, RMS rescale 0.18); AdamW for embedding, prediction head, and RMSNorm modules (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.95, eps=1e-20, weight decay 0.1). Flash: 32T tokens, batch 75.5M tokens, LR 2.7e-4 -> 2.7e-5 cosine, 2000-step warmup. Pro: 33T tokens, batch 94.4M, peak LR 2.0e-4 -> 2.0e-5. Sequence length curriculum 4K -> 16K -> 64K -> 1M; sparse attention introduced at 64K, lightning-indexer warmup at 64K. MTP loss weight 0.3 -> 0.1 at LR decay. Stability: Anticipatory Routing (routing indices from theta_{t-dt}, ~20% wall-clock overhead, auto-activated on loss spikes) + SwiGLU clamping (linear [-10,10], gate cap 10).
facts.source: arXiv 2606.19348 Sec 4.2.2 (Training Setups) + Sec 4.2.3 (Mitigating Training Instability, p25-26), read 2026-09-08
facts.boundary: training setup description, not our measurement

facts.value: Our checkpoints are NoPE: GatedMLA (model.py:227) carries no positional encoding, position is handled by KDA/DeltaRecurrence. DeepSeek-V4 uses partial RoPE on the last 64 dims (with a -i position correction on attention outputs). V4 ships the attention upgrade and the PE change together, and the -i correction exists because CSA's KV-as-values structure introduces absolute position -- so the coupling is likely structural, but the paper does not state that CSA requires partial RoPE. Adopting V4's partial RoPE still breaks checkpoint compatibility: the position-encoding dimensions change, so an existing NoPE checkpoint cannot be continued under the new scheme without a PE-conversion or a re-pretrain of the attention path. This is the cost of the CSA/HCA loop.
facts.source: our model.py:227 (GatedMLA docstring 'NoPE, KDA handles position', read 2026-09-08) + arXiv 2606.19348 Sec 2.3.3 (partial RoPE)
facts.uncertainty: the break is structural (different PE families); the cost of a conversion path is not measured
facts.boundary: cost statement for the next-version loop, not a measurement
